title: Tenses Quiz 3
description: Choose the right past form and watch the spelling of the verbs.
instructions: Tenses: Past simple and past continuous.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Yesterday I ___ to the market.'
questions.explanation: Go is irregular, so its past simple is went. Watch out: goed does not exist, and gone needs have or has.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: After did, the verb returns to the base form. Watch out: the past is already shown by did.

questions.question: They {{1}} TV last night. (not watch)
questions.explanation: The negative is did not + base verb. Watch out: not did not watched.

questions.question: I {{1}} (cook) when the phone {{2}} (ring).
questions.explanation: The longer action is in the past continuous, and the shorter action that interrupts it is in the past simple.

questions.question: Complete: 'While she ___, the lights went out.'
questions.explanation: While introduces an action in progress, so the past continuous is needed. Watch out: the other forms do not fit a story in the past.

questions.question: 'He stoped at the shop' is correctly spelled.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is stopped: the final p is doubled after a short vowel. Watch out: the same happens with plan, planned.

questions.question: Write the past simple of each verb.
questions.explanation: Each verb follows a spelling rule: consonant + y becomes -ied, a short vowel doubles, a final e just adds d. Watch out: play keeps its y because it follows a vowel.

questions.question: Match each verb with its past simple.
questions.explanation: These irregular verbs must be learned by heart. Watch out: bought and brought look alike.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The past continuous is was or were + -ing.

questions.question: Which sentence describes an interrupted action?
options: I have walked home since it started to rain.
I walk home every time it starts to rain.
I walked home, and then it started to rain.
I was walking home when it started to rain.
questions.explanation: The longer action (walking) is in progress when the shorter one (rain) happens. Watch out: the past simple alone shows two separate actions.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: He didn't went to school.
accepted: He did not go to school.
He did not go to school
questions.explanation: After did not, the verb is the base form go. Watch out: the past is shown only once.

questions.question: Which of these are irregular past simple forms?
questions.explanation: Played and worked just add -ed, so they are regular. Watch out: irregular forms change the verb itself.
